extracted.intended_audience: entry-level USPTO patent examiners and the general public (patent practitioners/applicants)
extracted.subtask_description: Computer-based training modules used to train entry-level patent examiners covering substantive patentability law, claim construction, search strategy, application formalities, and examination practice. Materials are also made available to the public for learning USPTO examination standards and procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent systems (forms of IP and who may apply)
rubrics_metrics.description: Learn the various forms of intellectual property and types of patents, who may apply for and what can be patented, and the USPTO's role in the U.S. government.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Overview module for understanding basic categories of IP, eligibility to apply, what subject matter can be protected, and the institutional role of the USPTO in examination and grant.

rubrics_metrics.name: 35 U.S.C. 101 (subject matter eligibility and related topics)
rubrics_metrics.description: Become more knowledgeable about 35 U.S.C. 101 and the following topics derived therefrom: statutory categories of invention, the utility requirement, eligible subject matter, and double patenting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers the statutory categories of invention and the utility/eligible-subject-matter analysis examiners must apply when determining whether a claimed invention is directed to patent-eligible subject matter under 35 U.S.C. 101.

rubrics_metrics.name: Double patenting
rubrics_metrics.description: Instruction on double patenting doctrine and how it interacts with 35 U.S.C. 101 and other examination considerations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Module titled 'Double patenting' to teach recognition and handling of double patenting issues (procedural and substantive approaches to resolving double patenting).

rubrics_metrics.name: Restriction practice / Unity of Invention
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognize when a restriction may be made under Unity of Invention and U.S. restriction practice and learn how to set up a restriction requirement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance for identifying independent and distinct inventions within a single application and the proper procedure for issuing a restriction requirement (including how to frame and document the restriction).

rubrics_metrics.name: Prior art rejections — general framework
rubrics_metrics.description: Build an understanding of 35 U.S.C. 102(a)(1), (a)(2), and (b), as well as 35 U.S.C. 103 and the corresponding concepts and analysis required for prior art rejections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers the overall analysis for making novelty and obviousness rejections, including what qualifies as prior art, how to make a prima facie case, and the rationales used to support obviousness rejections.

rubrics_metrics.name: 35 U.S.C. 102(a)(1) — prior art (public disclosures)
rubrics_metrics.description: Introduction to 35 U.S.C. 102(a)(1) and the rules governing prior public disclosures and their effect on novelty.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Module 'Introduction to 35 U.S.C. 102(a)(1)' focuses on assessing whether prior public disclosures anticipate claimed subject matter and the evidentiary/practical considerations for examiners.

rubrics_metrics.name: 35 U.S.C. 102(a)(2) — prior art (patent/applications as prior art)
rubrics_metrics.description: Introduction to 35 U.S.C. 102(a)(2) addressing when other patents or published applications can act as prior art against a claim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Module 'Introduction to 35 U.S.C. 102(a)(2)' explains the circumstances under which earlier-filed patents/applications qualify as prior art and how to apply filing-date related rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: 35 U.S.C. 102(b) — exceptions
rubrics_metrics.description: Introduction to 35 U.S.C. 102(b) exceptions and how statutory exceptions may affect prior art determinations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Module 'Introduction to 35 U.S.C. 102(b) exceptions' covers statutory grace-period and other exceptions and how they alter the prior art analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: 35 U.S.C. 103 — obviousness
rubrics_metrics.description: Instruction on 35 U.S.C. 103 and the rationales and analyses required for obviousness rejections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Split into multiple parts ('35 U.S.C. 103 Part 1/2/3') to cover the factual and legal framework for determining obviousness, making a prima facie case, and articulating rationales and motivation to combine references.

rubrics_metrics.name: 35 U.S.C. 112(a) — written description and enablement
rubrics_metrics.description: Explore 35 U.S.C. 112 section (a) and the corresponding concepts including written description and enablement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Module 'Introduction to 35 U.S.C. 112(a)' explains examiner expectations for the specification: sufficient written description to show possession of the claimed invention and enablement to teach making and using the invention without undue experimentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: 35 U.S.C. 112(b) and (d) — claim clarity and dependent claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Explore 35 U.S.C. 112 sections (b) and (d), focusing on claim clarity and proper dependent claim form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Module 'Introduction to 35 U.S.C. 112(b) and (d)' covers requirements for clear, definite claim language and correct structure/format for dependent claims and multi-part claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: 35 U.S.C. 112(f) — means-plus-function claiming
rubrics_metrics.description: Introduction to 35 U.S.C. 112(f) and analysis for means-plus-function claim language.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Module '35 U.S.C. 112(f) Introduction' teaches how to identify means-plus-function claim elements and the corresponding requirement to find adequate structure in the specification to support the claim under 112(f).

rubrics_metrics.name: Claim interpretation — broadest reasonable interpretation
rubrics_metrics.description: Learn how to give claims their broadest reasonable interpretation, including such topics as the effect of the preamble, functional language, intended use, and product-by-process claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Modules ('Claim interpretation Introduction' and Parts 1–2) provide guidance on applying the broadest reasonable interpretation standard, and on how specific claim features (preamble, functional language, product-by-process) affect claim scope and interpretation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Basic requirements to file and formalities
rubrics_metrics.description: Understand the basic requirements to file an application and formalities required by the USPTO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Module 'Basic requirements to file and formalities' covers required documents, filing fees, formal formatting, oath/declination, and initial procedural checks examiners and filers must observe.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent examiner role and application flow
rubrics_metrics.description: Develop an understanding of the role of the patent examiner and the flow of an application through examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Module 'Patent examiner and flow of an application' explains examiner responsibilities, stages of prosecution, timelines, and interactions with applicants (office actions, responses, interviews).

rubrics_metrics.name: Types of patent applications
rubrics_metrics.description: Learn about the different types of patent applications (e.g., provisional, nonprovisional, PCT, continuations) and their characteristics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Module 'Types of applications' helps distinguish filing routes, priority effects, and procedural differences among application types.

rubrics_metrics.name: Search strategy fundamentals
rubrics_metrics.description: Learn search strategy fundamentals to understand a repeatable approach for planning and conducting a complete and thorough search.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Module 'Search Strategy' provides a repeatable method for selecting search classes/databases, developing search queries, documenting search rationale, and ensuring a complete prior art search for examination.

rubrics_metrics.name: IDSs, after-final practice, and RCEs
rubrics_metrics.description: Develop an understanding of information disclosure statements (IDSs), after-final practice, and requests for continued examination (RCEs).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covered under 'General/Other' topics to instruct examiners on handling submitted prior art/IDSs, practice after final rejection (including when to allow reopenings or enter late papers), and the use and processing of RCEs.
